review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read Axis.lean, where axisHeight, axisHeight_zero and axisHeight_add are defined. I checked how these lemmas and the placedAxis, opposedAnchor and oppositeStep definitions are used in ShiftedBlocks, ReversedContacts, LateContacts, Main, ExperimentContact and ContactBins. A grep for `@[simp]` across the DirectionalWalk directory returned nothing, so the whole directory has no simp interface for the axis-height, placement and anchor API. I did not run Lean. The suggested simp sets are judged by inspection only. I did not check how they interact with other simp lemmas or with `omega`/`push_cast` steps in downstream proofs.

findings.declaration: axisHeight_neg / axisHeight_opposite / axisHeight_sum / axisHeight_step_self (axisHeight additivity API)
findings.excerpt:
lemma axisHeight_neg {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (x : Site d) :
    axisHeight e (-x) = -axisHeight e x := by
findings.problem: These are all structural push-in rewrites for axisHeight: negation, sum, the opposite step, and the step vector of the same direction. None of them is tagged @[simp], and neither are axisHeight_add or axisHeight_zero in Axis.lean. Every caller has to list them by hand, for example `simp [axisHeight_zero]` in axisHeight_sum, the long list at line 92 `simp [opposedAnchor,axisHeight_neg,axisHeight_add,axisHeight_sum,axisHeight_step_self,hp,hm,...]`, and the `rw [axisHeight_sum]`/`rw [sub_eq_add_neg,axisHeight_add,axisHeight_neg,htotal]` chains in ReversedContacts.lean. Each rule has a strictly smaller right-hand side (axisHeight applied to atoms), so tagging them would terminate. A related fact, axisHeight_step_opposite, sits in ContactBins.lean and is also not simp.
findings.proposed_change: Tag axisHeight_zero, axisHeight_add, axisHeight_neg, axisHeight_sum, axisHeight_opposite and axisHeight_step_self with @[simp], and axisHeight_step_opposite as well, moving it next to its neighbours. The cleaner alternative is to define `axisHeightHom e : Site d →+ ℤ` and state these lemmas as `map_add`/`map_neg`/`map_sum` instances, which simp already knows. Then drop the explicit lemma lists in opposedAnchor_height and in the ReversedContacts/ExperimentContact proofs. Keep `axisHeight_wordEnd` unsimp'd because it has hypotheses.
findings.benefit: Terms such as `-axisHeight e (opposedAnchor ...)` and `axisHeight e (∑ j ∈ range n, wordEnd (Z j))` normalise to sums of per-word heights by plain `simp`. Proofs no longer carry hand-maintained lemma lists, and the heights are in one canonical form, which `omega` and `push_cast` can then use.

evidence.excerpt: axisHeight e (x+y) = axisHeight e x + axisHeight e y

findings.declaration: placedAxis (missing equation simp lemmas) and placedWidth
findings.excerpt: def placedAxis {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (b : Bool) : Step d := if b then oppositeStep e else e
findings.problem: placedAxis is a def with an `if b`, and it has no simp lemmas for the literal cases `placedAxis e false` and `placedAxis e true`. Callers repeatedly unfold it and then clean up the `if`, using `simp only [placedAxis,Bool.false_eq_true,↓reduceIte]` and `simp only [placedWidth,placedAxis,↓reduceIte] at *`. This appears at lines 108, 110, 112 and 113 of this file, and again in Main.lean and LateContacts.lean. The `Bool.false_eq_true` and `↓reduceIte` bookkeeping is noise. It also unfolds placedWidth and placedAxis under `at *`, which is brittle for the later `omega` call.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma placedAxis_false (e : Step d) : placedAxis e false = e := rfl` and `@[simp] lemma placedAxis_true (e : Step d) : placedAxis e true = oppositeStep e := rfl`. Add matching `placedWidth_false`/`placedWidth_true` lemmas, which are `rfl` after those two. Then the case splits in opposed_departure_band can be `simp only [placedAxis_false, placedWidth_false] at ...`, and the callers in Main.lean and LateContacts.lean shrink too. Keep the definitions themselves non-simp so `placedAxis e b` for variable `b` stays folded.
findings.benefit: Unfolding is limited to the literal Bool cases. The `if` does not leak into hypotheses, and `at *` unfolding of placedWidth and placedAxis is no longer needed. Statements keep the readable `placedAxis e b` form, and the same lemmas can be reused in every file that currently repeats the unfolding recipe.

findings.excerpt:
def opposedAnchor {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (Z : TwoTape (Word d)) (b : Bool) (i : ℕ) : Site d :=
  if b then -stepVector e + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range i, wordEnd (Z (true,j))
findings.problem: opposedAnchor is defined by an `if b`, and every user unfolds it together with `Bool.false_eq_true`/`↓reduceIte`, in this file (lines 92, 149, 153), in ShiftedBlocks.lean:164 and in ReversedContacts.lean at lines 18, 111 and 122. There is no @[simp] equation lemma for `opposedAnchor e Z true i` or `opposedAnchor e Z false i`. There is also none for `opposedSite e Z b i t`, which is just anchor plus wordPath. Each proof therefore re-exposes the raw definition body and the if-reduction lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma opposedAnchor_true : opposedAnchor e Z true i = -stepVector e + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range i, wordEnd (Z (true,j)) := rfl` and `@[simp] lemma opposedAnchor_false : opposedAnchor e Z false i = -(∑ j ∈ Finset.range (i+1), wordEnd (Z (false,j))) := rfl`. Optionally add `opposedSite_def` as a plain lemma, not simp. Replace the `simp only [opposedSite,opposedAnchor,Bool.false_eq_true,↓reduceIte,...]` calls with these lemmas.
findings.benefit: Callers get simp lemmas that fire only on literal tapes. The `Bool.false_eq_true`/`↓reduceIte` boilerplate repeated across at least four files goes away. Proofs read as statements about the true tape and the false tape, and the generic `opposedAnchor e Z b i` stays folded when `b` is a variable.

findings.problem: The statement `axisDirection (oppositeStep e) = -axisDirection e` is the canonical way to push `oppositeStep` out. It is not simp, and the file has no companion lemmas such as `oppositeStep_oppositeStep`, `(oppositeStep e).1 = e.1`, or `axisHeight e (stepVector (oppositeStep e)) = -1`. Callers rewrite it by hand: `simpa only [placedAxis,↓reduceIte,axisDirection_opposite] using hh.2` in LateContacts.lean, and `axisHeight_step_opposite` in ContactBins.lean is proved by `rw [axisHeight_opposite]`. The proof itself is an unstructured `simp ... <;> split_ifs <;> norm_num` chain. Because `oppositeStep` has no simp lemmas, expressions such as `oppositeStep (oppositeStep e)` stay unsimplified.
findings.proposed_change: Mark axisDirection_opposite @[simp]. Add `@[simp] oppositeStep_oppositeStep : oppositeStep (oppositeStep e) = e`, and `@[simp] oppositeStep_fst : (oppositeStep e).1 = e.1` if needed. Together with the simp'd axisHeight_opposite from the first finding, this makes `oppositeStep` in an axis position normalise away. The orientation is safe because the right-hand side contains no `oppositeStep`.
findings.benefit: Terms mixing `axisDirection`, `axisHeight` and `oppositeStep` reduce to the base step `e` under `simp`. This removes the one-off `simpa only [..., axisDirection_opposite]` calls and gives a single normal form for the placed-axis API.
